sources_considered.why: Primary technical report from the ARC Prize organisers on 2025 results. It compares humans and AI on a general-reasoning benchmark and gives an explicit judgment on AGI.
Reports Musk's January 2026 Davos remark, which treats AI smarter than any human as still in the future.
Counterevidence context: strong 2025 AI performance in a narrow domain (IMO gold).
read_page returned a different page, so the text could not be quoted.
Forum post about 2026 ARC-AGI-2 scores, after the deadline. Not a primary source.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv (ARC Prize Foundation: Chollet, Knoop, Kamradt, Landers)

receipt.public_excerpt: By this definition, we have not yet achieved AGI.

evidence_items.explanation: The benchmark organisers judged that as of the end of the 2025 competition cycle there were still tasks easy for ordinary humans but hard for AI, so AGI had not been reached. That is consistent with no AI being smarter than every human by end of 2025.

receipt.public_excerpt: The top competition score reached a new state-of-the-art on the ARC-AGI-2 private dataset of 24% at a compute cost of $0.20 per task.

evidence_items.explanation: The same report says every ARC-AGI-2 task was solved by at least two untrained members of the public. The best 2025 competition entry scored 24% on the private set, so AI did not exceed every human on this general-reasoning test.

receipt.public_excerpt: “We might have AI that is smarter than any human by the end of this year, and no later than next year,” he stated

evidence_items.explanation: At Davos in January 2026, the person who made the original forecast still described AI smarter than any human as a future event (end of 2026 or 2027). This implies it had not arrived by the end of 2025.

receipt.public_excerpt: achieved gold medal performance at the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO), solving five out of six brutally difficult problems and earning 35 out of 42 possible points.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that AI matched elite humans in one narrow area in 2025. It solved five of six problems, which is not proof that it beat every human in general ability. It is listed as the strongest counterpoint.

unresolved_gaps: No single agreed test for 'smarter than any one human' exists. The finding rests on general-reasoning benchmark results and on statements by the benchmark organisers and by Musk himself.
Read on its own, ARC-AGI-2 tests only one kind of ability. Later reports (2026) of higher frontier-model scores fall after the deadline and were not used.
